column1: # P0 PREMISE (SND-1 as the review states it): original, then the merge rev 1 allows
# P1 WIN effects in m matter only where m can match the moved branch span: disjoint m holds
# P2 a lookaround holding a capture is a WIN effect
# P3 TRIAL effects: a callout fires when m is merely tried, even when m cannot match
# P4 TRIAL effects: backtracking verbs (libpcre2 only; pcrec refuses verbs, out of scope)
# P5 effect-free m: controls that must HOLD (lookahead, atomic, anchors, equal-width class)
# P6 only the MOVED branch is tested: m prefix-related to i but not j holds
# P6b control: m prefix-related to the MOVED branch j moves the answer (premise shape)
# P7 prefix key: a multi-way key with a callout in a rest changes the callout count; a class-sequence key does not
# P8 suffix factoring keeps the trial sequence: callouts in the shared tail
# P9 SND-5: prefix factoring inside a lookbehind body (pcrec refuses the factored form)
# P10 utf8 caseless: the same \K hazard at code-point level
